rows.title: Deep learning method for localization and segmentation of abdominal CT
rows.method: Deep Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision
rows.summary: No abstract was supplied, so the contribution cannot be extracted.

rows.title: Deep Learning with Domain Randomization in Image and Feature Spaces for Abdominal Multi-organ Segmentation on CT and MRI Scans
rows.method: Extended nnU-Net with domain randomization in image and feature spaces
rows.dataset: AMOS; unnamed public multi-institutional prostate MRI and abdominal CT/MRI datasets
rows.metric_values: Average DSC on unseen test domains: 88.22 versus TotalSegmentator 79.01 and MRSegmentator 75.84; both P<0.001
rows.summary: Combining image-space and feature-space domain randomization improves abdominal multi-organ segmentation accuracy and generalization across sites and modalities.

rows.title: The application of deep learning in abdominal trauma diagnosis by CT imaging.
rows.journal: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
rows.method: 2D semantic segmentation followed by 2.5D organ-injury classification
rows.dataset: Unnamed Kaggle competition dataset: 3,147 patients, including 855 with abdominal trauma
rows.metric_values: Renal injury: accuracy 0.932, PPV 0.888, NPV 0.943, sensitivity 0.887, specificity 0.944; liver injury: accuracy 0.873, PPV 0.789, NPV 0.895, sensitivity 0.789, specificity 0.895; spleen injury: accuracy 0.771, PPV 0.630, NPV 0.814, sensitivity 0.626, specificity 0.816
rows.summary: A segmentation-and-classification pipeline detects multiple abdominal organ injuries on CT for preliminary trauma screening.

rows.title: Annotation-free multi-organ anomaly detection in abdominal CT using free-text radiology reports: a multi-centre retrospective study.
rows.method: Multiple-instance learning using organ images from multi-organ segmentation and disease labels extracted from free-text radiology reports
rows.dataset: Private cohort: 66,684 training exams; 300 internal and 600 external validation exams, with data from three institutions for training/internal testing and six for external testing
rows.summary: Report-derived disease labels enable training of multi-organ abdominal CT anomaly detection models without manual disease annotations.

rows.title: Abdominal organ segmentation via deep diffeomorphic mesh deformations.
rows.method: UNetFlow: deep diffeomorphic template-mesh deformation with improved training and registration-based voxel–mesh alignment
rows.summary: UNetFlow reconstructs meshes for liver, kidney, pancreas, and spleen segmentation, improving generalization across organ geometries and supporting fine-tuning on new data.

rows.title: Fully-automated multi-organ segmentation tool applicable to both non-contrast and post-contrast abdominal CT: deep learning algorithm developed using dual-energy CT images.
rows.method: 3D nnU-Net trained on paired dual-energy CT portal venous phase and virtual non-contrast images
rows.modality: Dual-energy and single-energy CT, including non-contrast and post-contrast images
rows.metric_values: Mean DSC: liver, spleen, and each kidney >0.94; pancreas around 0.8; volume ICC: liver, spleen, and each kidney >0.95; pancreas 0.792 on SE-PVP and 0.840 on true non-contrast CT; volume error within 10% in >90% of cases for liver, spleen, and each kidney
rows.summary: Training on matched dual-energy CT images enables automated abdominal organ segmentation and volumetry across contrast conditions, with lower performance for the pancreas.

rows.title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning System for Segmentation of Abdominal Muscle and Fat on Computed Tomography.
rows.method: Fully convolutional network for automated muscle and fat segmentation
rows.modality: Axial CT at the inferior endplate of L3
rows.dataset: Private cohort: 883 training scans from 467 subjects; 426 internal validation scans from 308 subjects; 171 external validation scans from 171 subjects at two outside hospitals
rows.metric_values: Internal mean Dice: muscle 0.96, subcutaneous fat 0.97, visceral fat 0.97; external mean Dice: 0.97 for all three; internal mean area error: muscle 2.1%, subcutaneous fat 3.8%, visceral fat 1.8%; external mean area error: muscle 2.7%, subcutaneous fat 4.6%, visceral fat 2.3%
rows.summary: A fully convolutional network automatically segments abdominal muscle and fat on L3 CT images with high agreement against manual annotations in internal and external validation.

rows.title: External validation of a deep learning model for automatic segmentation of skeletal muscle and adipose tissue on abdominal CT images.
rows.method: Deep learning neural network for skeletal muscle and adipose tissue segmentation
rows.dataset: Private cohort: 3,187 abdominal surgery patients for training and 2,535 abdominal cancer patients for external validation
rows.metric_values: Median Dice: skeletal muscle 0.97 (IQR 0.95–0.98), visceral adipose tissue 0.98 (0.95–0.98), subcutaneous adipose tissue 0.95 (0.92–0.97); Lin's concordance: 0.964 (0.959–0.968), 0.998 (0.998–0.998), and 0.992 (0.991–0.993), respectively; Bland–Altman offsets: muscle radiodensity 0.23 HU (0.5%), muscle 1.26 cm²/m² (2.8%), visceral adipose tissue −1.02 cm²/m² (1.7%), subcutaneous adipose tissue 3.24 cm²/m² (4.6%)
rows.summary: An externally validated neural network automates L3 CT body composition analysis with strong agreement against expert muscle and adipose tissue segmentations.

rows.title: Deep-learning method for fully automatic segmentation of the abdominal aortic aneurysm from computed tomography imaging.
rows.method: Three-step deep learning pipeline extracting the aorta and iliac arteries followed by lumen and other aneurysm tissue segmentation
rows.summary: A fully automated deep learning pipeline segments abdominal aortic aneurysm tissues with qualitatively reported agreement against expert manual segmentation.

rows.title: A MultiRater MultiOrgan Abdominal CT Dataset for Calibration Analysis and Uncertainty Modeling in Segmentation.
rows.method: Dataset and benchmark for segmentation uncertainty and calibration; no specific AI architecture stated
rows.dataset: CURVAS: 90 scans from University Hospital Erlangen with pancreas, liver, and kidney segmentations annotated by three experts
rows.summary: CURVAS provides a multi-rater abdominal CT dataset for evaluating segmentation quality, uncertainty, calibration, and organ volumes while accounting for annotation variability.
